findings.element: [data-app="tasks"] .card[data-id="seam_n14_1"] .cardNote — produced at src/app.js:707 (cross()), rendered at src/tasks.js:450
findings.problem: The card the seam creates says the same sentence twice. Driving notes.seam at 1440 and pressing Send to Tasks then Open in Tasks lands a To Do card whose .cardTitle is "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" and whose .cardNote is "Switch on before guests arrive, not when." — identical but for the trailing full stop. The guard at src/app.js:707 is written to prevent exactly this (its own comment: "carries nothing at all when the title already IS them — a note that repeats its own title is noise") but it compares raw strings, and the peel keeps the sentence-final period while the task wording drops it, so the guard never fires. Every other card on the board pairs a title with a note that adds information; the one card the whole suite argument exists to produce is the one that stutters.
findings.fix: In src/app.js cross(), normalise both sides before comparing. Add above the api.add call: `var same = function (s) { return String(s || "").trim().replace(/[.,;:!?\u2026]+$/, "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").toLowerCase(); };` and change the note field to `note: entry.crossedWords && same(entry.crossedWords) !== same(entry.task) ? entry.crossedWords : "",`. The card then carries title, tag and the from-a-note mark only, which is what the comment already promises.

findings.element: api.reveal(id) at src/tasks.js:547 and reveal(target, el) at src/tasks.js:4123, driven from openTask() at src/app.js:735
findings.problem: The seam's payoff has no moment for a pointer user. Clicking Open in Tasks swaps to the board with no transition (sampled every 70ms from 60ms to 2700ms: animationName none, transform none, opacity 1, box-shadow exactly the resting card shadow rgba(17,17,17,.08) 0 0 0 1px …, outline 0px none) and appends the new card fourth in To Do with nothing at all to distinguish it from the other thirteen. api.reveal only clears filters, sets focusId and calls mount(); the horizontal reveal() only corrects scrollLeft. Driving the same flow entirely by keyboard DOES paint a 2px solid #4f46e5 outline plus a 4px rgba(79,70,229,.16) halo, because the ring is :focus-visible — so the one instant the whole suite is built to sell exists for the keyboard and is silent for the hand that will actually do it.
findings.fix: In api.reveal (src/tasks.js:547), after mount(), mark the card and let it announce itself in the palette already in use: `var el = window.__SUITE.host("tasks").querySelector('.card[data-id="' + id + '"]'); if (el) { el.classList.add("landed"); setTimeout(function () { el.classList.remove("landed"); }, 900); }`. In src/tasks.css add `@keyframes landed { from { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(79,70,229,.16), 0 0 0 1px rgba(79,70,229,.55); } to { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(79,70,229,0), 0 0 0 1px rgba(17,17,17,.08); } }` and `.card.landed { animation: landed .7s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1) 120ms both; }`, wrapped in the file's existing prefers-reduced-motion guard so the reduced-motion path holds the first frame for 700ms instead of animating.

findings.problem: The one object that is identical in all three products — the 17px/600 product wordmark with the indigo full stop — is the one object that moves when you change product. Measured from the shared white sheet's own top edge (all three sheets are the same box, 100,18): the wordmark's optical centre sits 31.0px down in Notes and 30.0px down in Tasks, and 52.8px down in Timeline. That is a 22px drop, identical at 1280, 1440 and 1920, plus a 12px shift right (28px inset in Tasks, 40px in Timeline) and a taller line box (25.5px vs 22.0px). Driving the rail from Tasks to Timeline, the indigo accent glides between slots as one liquid band — genuinely the best 200ms in the suite — and in the same beat the identity lurches down and right. The thing that should be nailed to the sheet is the thing that slides, which is the specific tell that reads as three sites behind one rail rather than one application.
findings.fix: In src/across.css:393, split the shorthand so the head's top padding is set to the head band's own rhythm rather than the stage's inset: `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead { padding: 18px var(--stage-pad) 0; }`. With the existing 25.5px line box that puts the wordmark's optical centre 30.8px below the sheet top, matching Tasks (30.0) and Notes (31.0) to within a pixel at every width. Keep the 40px left inset — it is the stage's real left edge and aligns the mark to the measure below it. Also add `line-height: var(--lead-tight)` (or whatever token yields the 22px box the other two use) to `[data-app="timeline"] .tlHead .word` at src/across.css:398 so the mark's box is the same height in all three products, then re-check the 18px against it.
